subject.title: Gateway runtime: "no such table: plugin_state_entries / acp_sessions" despite tables existing in state/openclaw.sqlite (agent turns produce no reply)

question: Should maintainers treat the newly merged container-startup checkpoint as enough to ask for a current-main retest, or require SQLite path diagnostics before selecting a fix boundary?
rationale: The source paths are clear, but the reported contradiction depends on the live process opening a different or partially initialized SQLite database; choosing a code fix before proving that path could patch the wrong layer.

options.title: Collect Path Proof First
options.body: Ask for redacted OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, resolved shared DB path, PRAGMA database_list, and gateway logs from a current-main or post-101881 image before opening a fix PR.

options.title: Retest PR 101881 Build
options.body: Ask the reporter to retest an image containing b81666ca6af25c86cc099983a4358cdc5ea9ced8 and close only if the fresh-volume table errors disappear.

options.title: Build A Focused Repro
options.body: Create a maintainer-owned Docker regression that exercises gateway run, device-pair polling, chat.history, and sessions.send under the reported env.

recommendation.title: Collect Path Proof First
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, resolved shared DB path, PRAGMA database_list, and gateway logs from a current-main or post-101881 image before opening a fix PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is about shared SQLite and ACP metadata ownership, where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
